from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Basis Vectors", [
            "Any 3D vector is a linear combination of basis vectors.",
            "Meet the standard basis: i, j, and k vectors.",
            "These define our 3D unit cube foundation."
        ])

        # Initialize ThreeDScene elements
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-1, 3], y_range=[-1, 3], z_range=[-1, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        i_hat = Vector([1, 0, 0], color="#FF5733")
        j_hat = Vector([0, 1, 0], color="#33FF57")
        k_hat = Vector([0, 0, 1], color="#3357FF")
        
        label_i = MathTex(r"\hat{i}", color="#FF5733").next_to(i_hat.get_end(), RIGHT)
        label_j = MathTex(r"\hat{j}", color="#33FF57").next_to(j_hat.get_end(), UP)
        label_k = MathTex(r"\hat{k}", color="#3357FF").next_to(k_hat.get_end(), UP+RIGHT)

        # Group components for positioning
        basis_group = VGroup(axes, i_hat, j_hat, k_hat, label_i, label_j, label_k)
        self.place_in_area(basis_group, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(i_hat), FadeIn(j_hat), FadeIn(k_hat))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(label_i), Write(label_j), Write(label_k))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        cube = Cube(side_length=1, fill_opacity=0.3, color=WHITE).move_to(ORIGIN)
        # Shift cube to match basis position logic
        cube.shift(basis_group.get_center() - ORIGIN)
        self.play(Create(cube))
        self.play(i_hat.animate.set_color(WHITE), j_hat.animate.set_color(WHITE), k_hat.animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining 3D Transformations", [

            j_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(ORIGIN, new_j),
            k_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(ORIGIN, new_k),
            run_time=2
        )

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The determinant represents a scaling factor for volume.",
            "Volume changes from V to V' under transformation.",
            "Determinant is the ratio V'/V.",

        ]

        # Define objects

        # Setup right-side area for 3D visualization
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(cube, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(axes), Create(cube))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        stretched_cube = Cube(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.7, color=GREEN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", [
            "3D transformations remap the entire 3D space grid.",
            "The matrix is a recipe for basis movement.",
            "Multiplication tracks complex character motion smoothly."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # 3D grid remapping
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2]).rotate(PI/4, axis=OUT).rotate(PI/6, axis=RIGHT)
        self.place_in_area(grid, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(grid), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Matrix as a recipe
        matrix = MathTex(r"\begin{pmatrix} a & b & c \\ d & e & f \\ g & h & i \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} = \mathbf{v}'")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(matrix), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Character motion representation (using a Sphere as placeholder for character mesh)
        sphere = Sphere(radius=0.5, color=BLUE).set_opacity(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(sphere.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.5 + UP * 0.5), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Basis Vectors (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Recall that any 3D vector [x, y, z] is a linear combination of basis vectors i, j, k. Introduce the standard basis: i=[1,0,0], j=[0,1,0], k=[0,0,1].
sections.example: Imagine a 3D unit cube sitting at the origin; its corners define the reach of our basis vectors.

sections.title: Defining 3D Transformations (0:45-1:45)
sections.content: A linear transformation is defined by where the basis vectors i, j, and k land. We represent this as a 3x3 matrix where columns are the transformed vectors i', j', and k'.
sections.example: An animation shows i, j, and k stretching and rotating into new positions while the grid space deforms accordingly.

sections.title: Core Concept: The Determinant (1:45-3:00)
sections.content: The determinant of a 3x3 matrix represents the 'scaling factor' of volume. If the volume of a shape changes from V to V', the determinant is V'/V.
sections.example: A virtual 'Robo-Dog' model is inside a unit cube. As we apply a transformation matrix, the cube (and the dog) stretches; if the determinant is 2, the dog appears twice as large in volume.

sections.title: Application: Rotation & Shear (3:00-4:15)
sections.content: Explain that different matrices perform different geometric operations: Rotations (preserving lengths/volumes) vs. Shear (sliding layers) vs. Scaling.
sections.example: Use a character's arm: A rotation matrix rotates the elbow joint, while a shear matrix mimics the 'squash and stretch' effect used in 3D animation to express motion.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis (4:15-5:00)
sections.content: Recap: Any 3D linear transformation is simply a remapping of the 3D grid. The 3x3 matrix is the 'recipe' for where the foundation vectors end up.
sections.example: A quick montage: A complex 3D character mesh transforming through a sequence of matrix multiplications, showcasing the final smooth motion.

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The basis vector animation encroaches on the left-side lecture text area, causing visual clutter. Fix: Line 5: self.place_in_area(basis_group, 'C4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.8) (line=5, object=basis_group)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Labels i, j, and k are poorly positioned relative to the vector origin and overlap with one another when the cube is rendered. Fix: Line 6: self.place_at_grid(i_label, 'D6', scale_factor=0.9); self.place_at_grid(j_label, 'C4', scale_factor=0.9); self.place_at_grid(k_label, 'D5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=6, object=basis_labels)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The unit cube foundation lacks clear spatial separation from the text block on the left. Fix: Line 7: self.place_in_area(unit_cube, 'D4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.7) (line=7, object=unit_cube)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The 3D transformation animation overlaps with the coordinate system axes and matrix equation, causing visual clutter. Fix: Line 61: self.place_in_area(three_d_obj, 'C4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5) (line=61, object=three_d_obj)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The matrix equation is positioned too centrally, creating tension with the text and the 3D animation space. Fix: Line 72: self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'D2', scale_factor=0.6) (line=72, object=matrix)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: Current layout fails to utilize the vertical space on the right, forcing all elements into a cramped quadrant. Fix: Line 61: self.place_in_area(three_d_obj, 'A4', 'C6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=61, object=three_d_obj)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Cube and axes overlap with the center and potentially interfere with readability. Fix: Line 61/62: self.place_at_grid(axes, 'D2', scale_factor=0.7); self.place_at_grid(cube, 'D2', scale_factor=0.6) (line=61, object=axes, cube)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Stretched cube animation occupies the same grid as original cube, causing visual clutter. Fix: Line 71: self.place_at_grid(stretched_cube, 'D4', scale_factor=0.7) (line=71, object=stretched_cube)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Formula is placed too high relative to the visual center, creating unbalanced negative space. Fix: Line 77: self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B4', scale_factor=0.9) (line=77, object=formula)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: Cube animation center is too close to the left text block, causing visual clutter. Fix: Line 57: self.place_at_grid(cube, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=57, object=cube)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: Matrix label is positioned too low, creating an unbalanced layout relative to the cube. Fix: Line 60: self.place_at_grid(matrix_tex, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=60, object=matrix_tex)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: Current layout ignores the 6x6 grid capacity, leading to poor spacing between the two primary assets. Fix: Line 61: self.place_in_area(group, 'B4', 'C6', scale_factor=0.9) (line=61, object=combined_assets)
[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: Matrix animation overlaps with the grid animation area. Fix: Line 64: self.place_in_area(matrix, 'D4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=64, object=matrix)
[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: Sphere is placed too close to the matrix, causing visual clutter. Fix: Line 71: self.place_at_grid(sphere, 'F2', scale_factor=0.6) (line=71, object=sphere)
[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: Grid visualization is too high, competing with the title header. Fix: Line 57: self.place_in_area(grid, 'B2', 'D6', scale_factor=0.4) (line=57, object=grid)
